ca_shangri_la.blurb: Shangri La is a small sport wall on Shuteye Ridge in the Sierra Nevada foothills, at roughly 7,000 feet. There are eight bolted routes, with one at 5.9, one at 5.10, four at 5.11 and two at 5.12. The wall is steep and faces east. Its rock carries multicolored streaks of lichen, and the climbing is technical crimping low down that turns to steeper pulling on big holds higher up. A short fixed line links the separate sections of the wall.

ca_sergeant_rock.blurb: Sergeant Rock is a crag in the Wonderland of Rocks section of Joshua Tree National Park, alongside the Wonderland Valley Trail at around 4,300 feet. Of its eight routes, seven are trad and one is sport. Grades run from an easy 5.5 up to 5.11, with four routes in the 5.10 range, which makes it a useful stop for climbers working at that level. Rock quality is fair to good.

ca_california_ridge.blurb: California Ridge is a mixed sport and trad crag in the western part of Castle Rock State Park in the Santa Cruz Mountains, at about 2,900 feet. It has eight routes: four sport, three trad and one top rope, spanning 5.6 to 5.12 with most around 5.10 and 5.11. Expect an offwidth, some face climbing and a few roofs studded with pockets. Routes are around 50 feet tall. Views reach out toward Monterey Bay, and the crag sees fewer visitors than the main rocks of the park.

ca_south_east_face.blurb: This is the moderate side of the Road Boulder, a single very large boulder in the Hartley Springs bouldering zone near June Lake, at around 8,200 feet in the Eastern Sierra. Eight problems cover the rounded wall, from V0 through V6, with the bulk between V0 and V3. The face suits climbers looking for straightforward problems and continuous movement. Landings slope and are not flat like most other boulders nearby, so bring pads and a spotter. To reach the face, hike up and around the back of the boulder; harder, more committing problems sit on the other sides.

ca_southern_blonde.blurb: Southern Blonde is a triangular, southwest-facing formation in the southern Alabama Hills outside Lone Pine, at about 4,700 feet on the Eastern Sierra side. Eight routes mix six sport lines with one trad route and one top rope. Grades stay between 5.8 and 5.10, with 5.10 being the most common, so it suits climbers building up from moderate routes. The base is a corridor, and a short boulder a little way up and right holds two additional bolted lines.

ca_sport_boulder_nw_face.blurb: This is the main face of the Sport Boulder at Thurman Flat in the San Bernardino Mountains, above Mill Creek along Highway 38 east of Redlands. It has eight bolted sport routes: one at 5.11 and seven in the 5.12 range. The boulder is steep and the climbing is fingery and powerful on routes that are short and well protected, so it is aimed at climbers comfortable around 5.12. The base sits close to the creek and can be underwater when the flow is high; the approach crosses the creek.

ca_sunset_cliffs_2.blurb: Sunset Cliffs is a set of buttresses and pillars within the Cemetery section of the Horsemen's Center climbing zone near Apple Valley in the High Desert. It holds eight climbs: five sport routes, one top rope and two boulder problems. Sport grades mostly run from 5.9 to 5.11, and the top rope is a 5.8. The cliffs face south, which makes them a good choice on days when shadier crags nearby are too cold. They lie southeast of Schlep Rock, along the way to the Stonehenge Boulders.

ca_stress_management_left.blurb: Stress Management Left is a boulder in the Emeralds bouldering zone of the I-80 corridor near Bowman, at about 5,000 feet in the Lake Tahoe region. It stands directly behind the slab-faced Stress Management Boulder, so you can find it by turning around from there. Eight problems are on it, ranging from very easy up to about V6, with most between V0 and V3. A lip traverse and a harder variation of it are the main features. The surrounding group is a handful of forest boulders.

_conflicts.ca_sport_boulder_nw_face: Stored rock is sandstone; the parent Thurman Flat page (https://www.mountainproject.com/v/109396018) says the boulder is polished conglomerate. Stored value left unchanged.
